subject: Autoscale SLO qualification - scale-up times & warm pools

Subject: Autoscale SLO qualification - scale-up times & warm pools

Hi Joe / Priya — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same definition for the SLOs and autoscale behavior we discussed.

Call highlights (summary):
- Target SLOs we discussed: request-level p95 latency <= 300ms (non-streaming), streaming token latency 99p <= 150ms.
- Baseline throughput: ~200 req/s steady; expected bursts up to 500 req/s (business-critical events).
- Concurrency: typical concurrent requests ~50, peak concurrent ~220 during bursts.
- Streaming requirements: clients expect immediate token streaming (server should start pushing tokens as generated).
- Autoscale/burst behavior: preference for warm-pool based bursts for fastest response; fall back to cold provisioning with acceptable scale-up time cap.

Technical assumptions we captured:
1) Warm pool size: target of 2-4 pre-warmed slots for the FastPay model family.
2) Warm slot readiness: model loaded and process healthy but KV cache empty — should allow token streaming immediately.
3) Scale-up target: for warm-pool consumption, sub-10s handoff to serve traffic; for cold provisioning we expect ~20-30s depending on model size and quantization.
4) Queueing: short front-end queue allowed (<= 5s) before rejecting; for streaming we prefer to start token streaming as soon as first tokens are available rather than delaying for model warm.

Requested artifacts / next steps (action items):
- Joe: share a 48h sample of traffic by hour and a short RPS histogram (thanks for uploading fastpay_workload_sample.csv).
- Redwood (Dev): provide an autoscale test plan — we propose a synthetic spike to 600 rps for 60s to observe scale behavior. (attached autoscale-test-plan.md)
- Marissa/Neha: draft SLA language for burst capacity and scale-up targets (attached redwood-autoscale-sla-draft.pdf)

Attachments: fastpay_workload_sample.csv (CSV sample), redwood-autoscale-sla-draft.pdf (draft SLA), autoscale-test-plan.md (test plan)

Proposed timeline: schedule autoscale test next week (preferably Wed or Thu morning PT). Please confirm availability and any additional constraints (data residency, retention, or compliance checks).

Thanks — I'll coordinate the test plan and invite the run owners.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — very helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side before we lock the test window:

1) When you say "streaming token latency 99p <= 150ms", do you mean per-token emit latency once the model has started generating, or end-to-end latency for the first token after request arrival? For our use case the first-token time matters (we want users to see response start within ~200ms ideally).

2) Scale-up target: FastPay requirement is that during billing spikes we must see page load-to-first-byte in <20s for 95% of requests. Can Redwood commit to a 20s SLO for scale-up from cold start, or do we need to rely on warm pools + extra warm slots?

3) We can shift the autoscale run to Thu morning PT — that works for our infra team. We'll validate we can reproduce a 600 rps spike on our side (burst injector ready).

Looping in Priya (our infra lead) for anything around network throttling / egress limits. Thanks — Joe

Hi all — quick engineering clarifications to set expectations and propose concrete test parameters.

Streaming vs first-token:
- We can provide a first-token SLA that is dominated by either warm-pool handoff or cold load time. For warm-pool served requests, first token can often be delivered in ~50-150ms depending on model step time and decoding. For cold starts the first-token time is the time to finish model load + init, which ranges by model size.

Scale-up behavior details:
- Warm pool: slots hold fully loaded model process (no user KV state). Warm handoff to route traffic to a warm slot is ~2-8s (mostly networking and router handoff).
- Warm slot spin-up: when we provision an additional warm slot from cold (i.e., expanding the warm pool), model load + init typical measured range: 8-18s for quantized 8-bit models (depends on model family and sequence length).
- Cold provisioning (no warm pool available): end-to-end readiness (model load + health checks) typically 20-35s for the FastPay model sizes we tested.
- Queueing policy: front-end will queue up to configurable threshold (default 5s). For streaming, we start emitting tokens as soon as the first token is generated; we won't wait for full model warm if the request can be routed to an already-running worker.

Concrete proposal for the test:
- Pre-warm config: set warm pool to 3 slots for the run.
- Traffic profile: baseline 200 rps for 5 mins -> spike to 600 rps sustained 60s -> drop to baseline.
- Observables: request-level p95/p99 latency, first-token time distribution, number of requests served by warm slot vs cold-provisioned slot, time to reach traffic target, queue durations, error rate.
- Success criteria (example): 95% of spike requests served with first-token <= 200ms and end-to-end p95 <= 350ms, no more than 10% of spike requests get rejected due to queue overflow.

I attached a short autoscale-test-plan.md with exact steps and the CLI commands we'll run from our side. If FastPay needs a stricter <20s cold-start SLO we should plan to rely on a warm pool at commit (or commit to a larger warm pool during business hours).

Let me know if you want us to run a pilot with different warm sizes (2, 3, 5) and we'll include that as separate runs.

Thanks,
Dev
